subtitle: Initial and boundary value problems, transforms and PDEs

chapters.title: First-Order ODEs

chapters.title: Second-Order Linear ODEs
chapters.summary: Second-order linear ODEs describe springs, masses, pendulums (for small angles), and RLC circuits. They are the most important ODEs in engineering.

sections.title: Turning one ODE into a system

chapters.title: Laplace Transforms
chapters.summary: The Laplace transform turns an ODE into an algebra problem. It is the best tool for IVPs with discontinuous or impulsive forcing, which are common in circuits and control.

chapters.title: Numerical Methods for IVPs
chapters.summary: Most real ODEs have no formula for the solution. We then compute the solution step by step on a computer. All methods in this chapter solve an IVP y' = f(x,y), \qquad y(x_0) = y_0 . We choose a step size $h$ and compute approximations $y_n \approx y(x_n)$…

chapters.title: Boundary Value Problems and Eigenvalues
chapters.summary: This chapter is the bridge from ODE to PDE. When we solve the wave, heat and Laplace equations by separation of variables (Part B), the ODE parts are boundary value problems. The key idea is the eigenvalue.

chapters.title: Fourier Series
chapters.summary: A Fourier series writes a periodic function as a sum of sines and cosines. We need it to fit initial conditions in PDEs. The eigenfunctions of Chapter 6 are exactly these sines and cosines.

chapters.title: Fourier Integrals and Transforms
chapters.summary: A Fourier series needs a periodic function on a finite interval. For a function on an infinite or half-infinite domain (a very long rod, a semi-infinite string) we use the Fourier transform. It is the limit of the Fourier series when the period goes to…

chapters.title: PDE Basics and Separation of Variables

chapters.title: Numerical Methods for PDEs
chapters.summary: When the region is irregular or the equation has variable coefficients, we solve PDEs on a computer. The standard tool is the finite difference method: replace derivatives by differences on a grid.

chapters.title: Series Solutions: Legendre and Bessel
chapters.summary: Some ODEs with variable coefficients have no solution in terms of $e^x$, $\sin x$ or powers. They appear when we solve PDEs in a sphere (Legendre) or a cylinder and a circular drum (Bessel). We solve them with power series.

chapters.title: Stability and the Phase Plane
chapters.summary: Often we do not need the exact solution. We only need to know: does the system settle down, blow up, or oscillate? This is stability. It is the main question in control, circuits and mechanics.

chapters.title: First-Order PDEs
chapters.summary: A first-order PDE has the unknown $z(x,y)$ and its first derivatives only. We use the common shorthand p = \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}, \qquad q = \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}.
